name: manual_aec0ea
claim: Agent-tool subagents run with isolation:'worktree' can see a STALE checkout of the branch relative to the orchestrating session's real-time state, and can hallucinate confident, specific-looking false claims from that staleness rather than reporting uncertainty. Observed: a subagent claimed 'this worktree's HEAD (65916c81) is a stale snapshot; main already carries commit 60636ad5 (P9 reorder buffer...)' -- but 60636ad5 was the orchestrating session's OWN just-pushed commit on a feature branch, never on main at all (git merge-base --is-ancestor 60636ad5 origin/main confirmed NO). The subagent's worktree checkout was simply behind the live branch tip; it inverted that into a false 'you're behind main' narrative stated with full confidence and specific SHAs, not hedged.

decisions.notes: Observed 2026-07-12 during a /autoplan CEO-review subagent dispatch. Verified false via direct git commands before trusting it -- per the standing AFRP anti-handwaving rule, a subagent's confident claim with specific-looking evidence (real SHAs, real commit messages) is not automatically ground truth if it could stem from stale/isolated state. Always verify a subagent's git-state claims directly (branch --contains, merge-base --is-ancestor) before acting on 'you're out of sync with main' style findings, especially from worktree-isolated agents.
